transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03
Time: 08:00 PT (scheduled 30m, ran 36m)
Duration: 36 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morris (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Mei Tan (HarborEdge), Ravi Singh (HarborEdge), Jordan Lowe (HarborEdge)

Auto-generated summary: Discussed renewal amendment to add APAC edge capacity, tradeoffs between dedicated vs hosted burst, security expectations and a short APAC benchmark. Action items captured.

[00:00] Lena Morris: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — happy Tuesday. Quick roll call, I think we have Mei, Ravi and Jordan from HarborEdge?
[00:12] Mei Tan: Yep, Mei here. Morning all.
[00:15] Ravi Singh: Ravi on our side.
[00:18] Jordan Lowe: Jordan here.
[00:20] Lena Morris: Great. Quick agenda: renewal amendment options, APAC edge onboarding, security questions, and a small benchmark. We'll keep it tight. Carlos, want to start on capacity options?
[00:28] Carlos Ruiz: Yeah for sure. So the main levers we talked about in the last deck — you can either add a dedicated pool in APAC or use hosted burst with regional routing. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower p50 token latency at scale, hosted burst is cheaper for spiky traffic. There's also the hybrid we call 'reserved + burst' where you keep a small dedicated baseline and burst to hosted when needed.
[00:54] Mei Tan: Can you remind us of the rough price delta? Last time the number we saw had a pretty big delta once you factor in baseline commit.
[01:05] Carlos Ruiz: Absolutely. Roughly, dedicated baseline is about 2.3x the unit cost versus hosted for baseline committed capacity, but that's for heavy steady throughput. If your traffic is spiky, hosted burst end up cheaper overall. I'll send a sample TCO with our estimator; Lena will include it in the amendment.
[01:25] Ravi Singh: We have two use cases: interactive customer-facing chat and offline batch embedding jobs for analytics. Chat needs low tail latency in APAC — that's the big driver.
[01:35] Lena Morris: Right, and chat is where dedicated helps with p95/p99. We can posture a small dedicated pool for chat and burst embeddings to hosted. That usually hits the unit-cost vs latency sweet spot.
[01:46] Jordan Lowe: On the security front, we need VPC peering or a private connectivity option. We're also mandated to use our HSM-backed KMS for key material. Is that supported in Private deployments only?
[02:00] Carlos Ruiz: Good question. We support customer-managed KMS integration both for Private and Dedicated in most regions; hosted also supports envelope encryption but not always direct HSM-backed keys per se — depends on the region and the cloud provider. For APAC we can do a Private control-plane or Dedicated within the customer's VPC if you need full KMS/HSM in-line. We'll include the specifics in the security pack.
[02:22] Jordan Lowe: Okay, that helps. We also need audit logs persisted for 12 months and SSO via SAML.
[02:30] Lena Morris: We have the audit log retention as an add-on; we'll map SAML/SSO centrally. We'll attach our SOC 2 report excerpt and the audit log diagram in the security pack (link below).
[02:40] Mei Tan: One more on latency: can we run a short benchmark in APAC to see p50/p95 with the chat prompt sets? We want something representative — maybe 100k tokens/day for a week?
[02:52] Carlos Ruiz: Totally. We can provision a test endpoint in Singapore for you, share test tokens and a Grafana dashboard. If you'd like, we can also run a tiny canary with a dedicated baseline for 24 hours to compare.
[03:06] Ravi Singh: That sounds good. Timeline-wise, our renewal is end of August, so we'd like the amendment finalized by the second week of August to get PO through finance.
[03:16] Lena Morris: Understood — the amendment timeline is tight but doable. We'll prioritize sending an amendment with two SKU options: (A) Dedicated baseline APAC + hosted burst for embeddings, (B) Fully hosted with regional routing + higher burst allowance.
[03:30] Jordan Lowe: What about fallbacks — if APAC capacity is constrained, do you have automated routing to other regions to avoid errors?
[03:37] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, smart routing can failover to another region or a compatible model variant. There is a short latency penalty but the call won't fail. We generally recommend fallbacks for customer-facing flows.
[03:48] Mei Tan: Ok. On compliance: do you have SOC2 type II? Our compliance team will want that before sign-off.
[03:55] Lena Morris: We do — SOC2 Type II — and we can share the attestations plus a redacted control matrix. We'll put that in the security pack link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack.pdf (provisional link).
[04:10] Ravi Singh: Competitors like CloudLarge told us they can do a region-only onboarding in 48 hours but their latency numbers were noisy. Anything we should watch for in the benchmark?
[04:21] Carlos Ruiz: Watch for cold-starts, KV cache behavior with long context, and model variant fallbacks. Also tokenization differences across providers can skew token counts; we'll baseline with your canonical prompts.
[04:36] Mei Tan: Sounds good. For the benchmark we want the exact prompts and conversation state to be preserved across runs — can you ensure KV caching settings mirror our production config?
[04:49] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, we'll mirror your seq lengths and cache TTL. If you can share sample prompts and average seq lengths that will help.
[04:57] Jordan Lowe: We'll share a redacted prompt set. On encryption, our legal wants to ensure logs containing user identifiers are scrubbed. Is there a PII redaction option?
[05:08] Lena Morris: We offer configurable redaction and token-level redaction can be applied at ingestion. We'll send the configuration doc.
[05:16] Ravi Singh: Budget-wise, if we go dedicated baseline in APAC, what kind of uplift to expect relative to our current commit? We currently have a US-focused commitment and about 20% spike in APAC traffic expected during our launch window.
[05:30] Carlos Ruiz: Roughly, a regional dedicated pool sized for baseline chat will add ~18–30% to your existing spend depending on model family and quantization profile. We'll produce a modeled range in the amendment and include quantization recommendations to reduce unit cost.
[05:46] Mei Tan: Are quantized model variants recommended for chat use cases at low latency? I've seen tradeoffs in quality before.
[05:53] Carlos Ruiz: There's a tradeoff: int8 quantization can be fine for many chat flows, but for higher-quality responses or longer-context reasoning we recommend int8 with per-channel scaling or int4 research profiles — our Optimize team can advise per-prompt. We'll flag quality regression risk in the docs.
[06:12] Lena Morris: Quick check — Jordan, for KMS/HSM, do you need a fully on-prem HSM or cloud HSM with Bring Your Own Key?
[06:20] Jordan Lowe: We need cloud HSM BYOK integrated with our KMS provider. On-prem HSM is tough with their networking scoping.
[06:27] Carlos Ruiz: BYOK cloud HSM is supported for Dedicated and Private control plane; we'll call out the exact cloud provider mappings in the pack.
[06:35] Mei Tan: Great. Logistics: tentative benchmark window next Monday through Friday? We can do low-volume mornings and higher-volume afternoons to simulate regional spikes.
[06:44] Ravi Singh: Agreed. Also want to confirm SLA for Dedicated — p99 latency objective?
[06:50] Lena Morris: Our Dedicated SLA covers availability and throughput — latency SLOs are target p95/p99 ranges and are tied to the model plus sequence length. We'll include the SLA appendix in the amendment.
[07:02] Carlos Ruiz: Adding — for the benchmark, we'll capture p50/p95/p99, tail distribution and error rates. We'll also log token cost and request IDs for traceability.
[07:13] Mei Tan: Perfect. A couple of quick questions from procurement: do you accept Net-45? We usually do Net-30 but could extend for enterprise vendors.
[07:23] Lena Morris: Standard is Net-30, but we can discuss Net-45 for enterprise deals — that usually goes through our finance team and might require an amendment. I'll flag it in the paperwork.
[07:33] Ravi Singh: On billing, will APAC capacity be a separate line item? It's easier for us for cost allocation.
[07:39] Lena Morris: Yes we can split line items by region and SKU for internal chargeback. We'll make sure the amended quote has region-level breakdowns.
[07:48] Jordan Lowe: One more: do you do penetration testing or will Redwood provide a test plan we can run against the APAC test endpoint?
[07:57] Carlos Ruiz: We provide a security test plan and can accommodate customer pentest scheduling after a short threat model review. We'll include the test plan in the security pack.
[08:08] Mei Tan: Thanks. Anything else on the commercial side?
[08:12] Lena Morris: Not from me. I'll summarize decisions: Redwood to send amendment with two SKU choices, provide security pack and test endpoint, and run APAC benchmark next week. HarborEdge to share prompt set and internal PO timing.
[08:25] Ravi Singh: That matches our expectations. If we can get the amendment by Friday that's ideal.
[08:29] Lena Morris: We'll aim for Friday; action items will be in the follow-up thread.
[08:33] Jordan Lowe: Quick note — competitor FathomAI mentioned a cheaper quoting structure but didn't support KMS BYOK which is a non-starter for us.
[08:41] Carlos Ruiz: Right, security is often the differentiator. We'll make the integration doc clear.
[08:46] Mei Tan: Great. Thanks everyone.
[08:48] Lena Morris: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the amendment and links. Talk soon.
